title: Better Auth: an introduction
partialText: What Better Auth is and how it works: the auth instance, the database schema, the catch-all route, and the client. Authentication for TypeScript apps, explained.

title: Cloudflare Artifacts: Git storage built for AI agents
partialText: Learn how Cloudflare Artifacts gives AI agents isolated Git repositories, short-lived access tokens, forks, and a programmable Workers API.

title: Cloudflare Drop: drag a folder, get a live site
partialText: Cloudflare Drop deploys a static site by dragging a folder or zip into the browser. No account, no CLI. How it works and how it ties into temporary accounts.

title: Temporary Cloudflare accounts: agents can now deploy without signing up
partialText: wrangler deploy --temporary deploys a Worker with no Cloudflare account. Live for 60 minutes, claimable with a link. How it works and its limits.

title: Workers Cache: a cache in front of your Cloudflare Worker
partialText: Cloudflare launched Workers Cache, a tiered cache that sits in front of your Worker. How to enable it, set Cache-Control headers, and purge by tag.

title: Moondream 3.1 on Workers AI: fast vision at the edge
partialText: Cloudflare brings the Moondream 3.1 vision model to Workers AI. Caption images, ask questions, get object coordinates and bounding boxes — in under a second.

title: inferencecost.dev: what will AI inference cost you at 10k users?
partialText: I built inferencecost.dev, a calculator for the biggest line item in AI product budgets: LLM inference. Compare ~30 models under your workload assumptions.

title: Sitebase: all the features your website needs, in one place
partialText: I'm building sitebase.dev: waiting lists, forms, newsletter signups, analytics, uptime monitoring and more, embedded in any site with one script. Currently in private beta.

title: StackPlan: figure out where to deploy your app, and what it'll cost
partialText: I built stackplan.dev, a deployment stack advisor. Describe your app, get a recommended hosting stack with real cost estimates. Why I built it and how.

title: How the Cloudflare Pages build cache works
partialText: How the Cloudflare Pages build cache speeds up deploys, which directories it restores for each framework, and how to keep your own caches between builds.

title: The Summer of Code
partialText: July and August: no new courses, no launches, just building. A recap of the first week: StackPlan, 140+ free tools, Sitebase, the bootcamp platform, and a new 30 Days of Code course.

title: How I generate an Open Graph image for every post
partialText: How I generate a unique Open Graph preview image for every blog post at build time in Astro, using astro-og-canvas, instead of one shared image.

title: New: 90 free tools for developers
partialText: I launched a new tools section on the site: 90 free calculators and utilities for developers, running entirely in your browser. No signup, no ads.

title: How I added search to my static site with Pagefind
partialText: How I added fast client-side search to my static Astro blog with Pagefind, which indexes your HTML at build time and runs entirely in the browser.

title: How to rebuild a Cloudflare site on a schedule
partialText: Learn how to rebuild a Cloudflare Pages site on a schedule using a deploy hook, triggered either by a GitHub Action cron or a Cloudflare Worker cron.

title: Cloudflare Email Workers: run code when an email arrives
partialText: How to receive and process incoming email with Cloudflare Email Workers, parse it with postal-mime, and forward or act on it.

title: Cloudflare Turnstile: stop bots without annoying CAPTCHAs
partialText: How to protect a form from bots with Cloudflare Turnstile. Add the widget to your page and verify the token from a Worker.

title: Cloudflare Workers: secrets and environments
partialText: How to handle config, secrets, and multiple environments (staging, production) in Cloudflare Workers without leaking anything.

title: Cloudflare Workers observability: logs and traces
partialText: Learn how to see what your Cloudflare Worker does in production using console.log, observability in wrangler.jsonc, and live tailing with wrangler tail.

title: Cloudflare Analytics Engine: store and query metrics
partialText: How to write custom events from a Worker with Analytics Engine and query them later with SQL. Cheap, high-volume time-series data.

title: The AI Workshop (July 2026 cohort)
partialText: The AI Workshop July 2026 cohort covers agents, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, MCP, skills, subagents, and practical AI workflows.

title: Cloudflare Cron Triggers: run a Worker on a schedule
partialText: How to run a Cloudflare Worker on a schedule with Cron Triggers. Nightly jobs, periodic checks, and cleanups, with no server to keep running.

title: Cloudflare Durable Objects: state that lives in one place
partialText: What Durable Objects are and how to use them, with their built-in SQLite storage. A simple counter and a rate limiter, explained from scratch.

title: Cloudflare Queues: run work in the background
partialText: How to use Cloudflare Queues to do work after the response is sent. Producers, consumers, batching, retries, and dead letter queues.

title: Cloudflare R2: object storage without egress fees
partialText: How to store and serve files like images and uploads with Cloudflare R2 from a Worker. S3-compatible storage with no egress fees.

title: Cloudflare KV: a key-value store for your Workers
partialText: Learn how to use Cloudflare Workers KV, an edge key-value store, to create a namespace and put and get data, ideal for sessions, feature flags and caching.

title: Cloudflare D1: a SQL database for your Workers
partialText: How to create a D1 database, manage its schema with migrations, and query it from a Worker. SQLite, served from the edge.

title: Serving a website with Cloudflare Workers static assets
partialText: How to deploy a static site, an SPA, or a full Astro app on Cloudflare Workers using the static assets feature, with a Worker for the dynamic parts.

title: Wrangler: the Cloudflare Workers command line tool
partialText: A practical guide to Wrangler, the CLI you use to build, run, deploy, and manage Cloudflare Workers and everything attached to them.

title: Executor: one gateway to connect your AI agent to every tool
partialText: A look at Executor, an open-source, local-first layer that gives your AI agents one shared catalog of tools, with shared auth and built-in safety rules.
